headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Uptrend holds, but leverage is crowding back in

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The market is in an early uptrend and signal confidence is high (73/100), so the posture is to increase acquisition spend, weighted toward active-trader and non-stablecoin channels that historically respond best in this phase. The caution is that leveraged traders have crowded back in quickly, which in past cycles has made sharp, short-lived pullbacks more likely, and the long-term average has not yet turned up. That argues for scaling up in steps and keeping some budget in reserve. This is a budget-posture view built on trailing data, not trading advice and not a forecast.

reasons: BTC is about 20% above its 200-day average after a +35% 90-day gain.
Fear & Greed at 70 (Greed) and leveraged traders paying up to stay long.
Spot ETFs added about $190M on the latest day; signal confidence 73/100.
Caveat: the 200-day average is still falling and price is 31% below its peak.
watch: The main tension is that leverage has rebuilt faster than the trend underneath it. Traders are paying an above-normal premium to bet on rises just days after a $434M long flush, while only about half of recent days closed above the long-term average and that average is still sloping down. The read would firm up if that premium cooled without price losing ground; it would weaken if another long flush pushed both leverage and the mood gauge lower together.
analysis: Bottom line: Bitcoin is still in an early uptrend, and the near-term mood is the strongest part of the picture, but that strength rests partly on borrowed money. Short term, the mood is clearly warm and close to frothy: the Fear & Greed gauge sits at 70 (Greed), and traders are again paying an above-normal premium to hold leveraged bets on rises, a sharp swing from paying to bet on falls only a few days ago. That swing follows a choppy week in which a failed push near $87,000 wiped out about $434M of mostly long positions on 3 October (CoinGlass data via The Crypto Times). The lean would firm up if that premium cooled while price held; another long flush would cut it quickly, and that is when newer, momentum-chasing users tend to pull back first.

Over the next month, the lean is mildly positive and softer than it was a day ago. Price is up about 35% over three months, but only about half of recent days closed above the long-term average, so the gain has been narrow rather than broad-based, and price has spent roughly two weeks stuck below its September high. The next scheduled event is the Federal Reserve meeting on 27–28 October. A clean break above the recent range with more days holding above the average would strengthen this; slipping back toward the low $80,000s would weaken it.

Long term, the picture is positive but still under construction. Price sits about 20% above its 200-day average, yet that average itself is still drifting down and Bitcoin remains about 31% below its all-time high, so this is a recovery inside a larger slump rather than a new-high market. Big-money demand is a steady support, with spot ETFs taking in about $190M on the latest day, while US 10-year borrowing costs near 5.3% remain the main headwind. The long-term case strengthens once the 200-day average turns up; a slide back toward that average with yields still high would weaken it, which argues for building long-horizon campaigns in stages.

team_notes.marketing: Lean into active-trader and non-stablecoin channels: a +35% three-month move and Bitcoin's strongest Q3 since 2017 give a factual growth story, and steady spot ETF inflows support an institutional-adoption angle. With the mood gauge at 70 and leveraged longs crowding back in after a $434M flush last week, avoid FOMO or urgency hooks and lead with education and risk-management features, while keeping stablecoin-first channels defended since the rally is still narrow.
